title: Never Squish the 30-Legged Bug in Your House
tiktok_caption: house centipede part 2 🐛 it hunts the bed bugs and roaches in your house. Would you let it stay? 🐛 stay / 🙅 squish

beats.say: You just saw the thirty-legged bug in your bathroom.
Don't squish it. It's hunting.
It eats bed bugs and baby cockroaches.
Silverfish. Spiders. Flies.
Squish it, and they all stay.
It stings its prey with legs that turned into fangs.
Will it sting you? Almost never. Only if you grab it hard.
It would rather run. It's one of the fastest things in your house.
And it hunts at night, while you sleep.
Most people never even see theirs.
So the one you just saw? It's working for you.
Its long feelers look just like its legs.
So a predator can't tell which end is the face.
A baby hatches with only four pairs of legs.
It grows more every time it molts, until it has fifteen pairs.
It takes about three years to grow up, and it can live up to seven.
And the female's back legs are almost twice as long as her body.
They hide by day in basements, cellars and bathrooms.
Bug experts say don't bother spraying it.
Dry out the damp spots, and the bugs it eats move out.
Fewer bugs, fewer centipedes. So, would you let it stay?
Follow me. Next: the bug that's older than dinosaurs.
